md_docs_2browser-upload-quality(3) Library Functions Manual md_docs_2browser-upload-quality(3)

NAME

md_docs_2browser-upload-quality - Browser upload quality

Compressed browser uploads use local transport feedback rather than a fixed width * height * 2 * fps bitrate. UploadQuality bounds the initial target to 64 kbit/s–8 Mbit/s at 0.12 bits per source pixel per frame. Requested capture dimensions and FPS remain ceilings; this controller never changes the camera track, source selection, or user settings. Raw uploads and local browser-host input retain their existing paths.

Every 500 ms, queued bytes above 64 KiB, queued video older than 60 ms, or a new outbound drop reduce the network target by 35%, down to 4% (with a final 32 kbit/s floor). Encoder backlog instead reduces the compute target by 20%, down to 20%, without treating a busy encoder as a slow network. The lower target selects spatial tiers of 100%, 75%, 50%, or 25%, and reduces FPS down to 5 (or the requested ceiling when lower). Five healthy seconds restore five percentage points, so recovery cannot immediately refill a recently congested link.

The encoder scales frames internally and recreates/probes the exact Annex B configuration when quality changes. Generation checks reject old output; each configuration begins with a keyframe and reset flag. Existing outbound queue admission, audio/control reserves, priority/barriers, 100 ms application video expiry, and keyframe recovery remain authoritative. Feedback is collected before capture backpressure can skip a frame, including after WebRTC host promotion. Bitrate-only changes need a 25% shift to recreate the encoder; full recovery always reapplies the original bitrate ceiling even when the final step is smaller. Adaptive probes keep the active encoder running until a replacement configures successfully. Unsupported tiers and candidate configuration failures retain the working codec, dimensions, and FPS, and rejected configurations are cached (up to 64 per session) to prevent a probe on every frame. Stopping capture invalidates pending probes as well as pending encoder output.

This policy belongs beside WebCodecs: browser capture frames and JavaScript transport queues do not traverse the C encoder. Moving the policy into C would add a WASM call boundary without sharing a current native encoding path. No wire format or native encoder behavior changes are needed.

Evidence

From web/web:

pnpm exec vp test run tests/network/upload-quality.test.ts tests/network/h265-encoder.test.ts tests/network/outbound-queue.test.ts
pnpm exec playwright test --config playwright.adaptive.config.ts

The browser test requires installed Chrome with H.264 WebCodecs support. It uses real encoding, decoding, and a visible received canvas, with an in-process shaped ordered link (3 Mbit/s, then 120 kbit/s for ten seconds, then recovery). Synthetic 20 ms audio packets share the actual OutboundQueue. The test records quality, decoded frame age, audio packet count, and maximum receive gap in test-results/*/collapse-recovery.json, plus adaptive-upload.png. This proves codec/queue behavior, not microphone playback, native networking, or physical network shaping. Full ceiling recovery is covered with deterministic policy time; the 34-second browser scenario checks gradual partial recovery.

An already submitted reliable transport packet cannot be recalled. Sudden collapse can therefore delay audio behind that packet even though queued audio has priority over subsequent video. The test bounds and reports this transient gap rather than claiming zero delay or end-to-end bandwidth estimation.
